- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the last 24 days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to previous day’s forecast.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0), model tends to underestimate; increase forecast by 1–3% relative to previous day’s forecast.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior day), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply a 2–5% downward correction to subsequent forecasts.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >85, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until price stabilizes; if <75, adjust upward by 1–2% per day.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lag: if true outcome shows strong upward trend, model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day lagged true values.
- When sentiment history shows a sudden spike (e.g., 0.5), model often overreacts; cap forecast increase at +2% from prior day’s forecast.
